text:
maya: heads up — ran a quick smoke on the new autotuner presets targeting L4/T4/A10. found an odd fallback path for short-seq (<64) prompts on T4 where it chooses the generic matmul kernel instead of the fused attention kernel.

jordan: ugh that explains the latency blip I saw in canary yesterday, ~20% higher p95 for some routes. any repro snippets?

maya: repro is simple. run this small bench: ```python
# minimal repro
for seqlen in [8,16,32,64]:
    run_infer(model='mpt-7b', device='t4', seqlen=seqlen, batch=2, kernel_preset='autotune')
```

kevin: can you paste the profiler stack for seqlen=16? curious if kv-cache hotpath is forcing different codegen.

maya: profiler snippet (trimmed): ```
seqlen=16, batch=2, device=T4
- forward total: 42.1ms
- fused_attention (skipped): 0ms
- matmul_generic: 28.3ms
- kv_cache_append: 3.1ms
- kernel_dispatch_decision: 1.2ms
```

tara: interesting — on A100 same config picks fused_attention and forward ~24ms. So autotuner is doing architecture-aware picks but has a threshold bug for <32 on compute-smaller GPUs.

jordan: is the decision based on estimated flops or on measured microbenchmarks? our autotuner should prefer measured microbenchmarks per-device+seqlen.

maya: current logic: prefer microbench if we have recent samples, else fall back to cost model that multiplies flops by device_score. Looks like T4 microbench table is stale for fused_attention at small seq.

kevin: could be due to the microbench sampling window — we avoid sampling very short seqlens because noise. but for T4 that noise is smaller relative to fused gain, so we missed it.

maya: quick patch idea: when device.family in ["T4","L4","A10"] and seqlen <= 32, force a microbench sample at cold-start and record median of 5 runs. cheap and should correct picks.

jordan: +1. also add a safety net: if chosen kernel has >15% regression vs last-known best, fallback to previously best kernel for next 10s. avoids noisy degradations in production.

kevin: agree. we should also check KV cache behavior — on T4 we saw kv_cache_append is relatively higher percent which may change batching heuristics. maybe reduce batch max for seqlen<32 on those GPUs.

tara: caveat: reducing batch cap will increase RPC overhead for hosted customers. we need to only toggle this for Dedicated/private where we control throughput, or make it a per-route override.

maya: plan: 1) implement forced microbench for short seqlen on T4/L4/A10, 2) add transient regression fallback, 3) add opt-in short-seq batch cap in runtime config, 4) run cluster sweep and collect perf traces.

jordan: can you open a short PR with the microbench + fallback flags? label it perf/critical. I'll allocate a canary on a T4 node pool.

maya: will do. tagging infra-bot to schedule canary once PR lands.
